rv.q: Aaron is a wonder to behold, balancing Marie’s conflicting emotions and beliefs.
By play’s end you will have laughed hard, cried uncontrollably and grown wiser in the process.
Lombardo’s tightly-paced play is not looking to break any new ground in personal plays about moms, but it earns the emotional beats.
This is an excellent entertainment for this dark time of year.

Mr. Lombardo and director Noah Himmelstein sustain a light comedic tone throughout; the writer acknowledges, with a wink, that his forays into slightly deeper waters haven’t endeared him to all reviewers.
The result is a breezy, enjoyable two-hander that benefits from the natural rapport generated by its immensely appealing stars, Caroline Aaron and Matt Doyle.
But most of the time, we know what Lombardo’s doing before he even does it.
As boulevard entertainments go, Conversation with Mother is often creepy rather than charming.
Conversations with Mother is a laugh-out-loud funny, sharply insightful, and deeply touching tribute to the complex, close-knit, cherished connection between a parent and child...
In these capable hands, Conversations with Mother finds a strong rhythm that engages and makes me wish for a similar kind of alignment that this mother-son pairing has found.
Ms. Aaron and Mr. Doyle can overcome the shortcomings of the material and deliver the comedic goods with ease and perfection.
I wasn’t able to connect to the characters, but I did thoroughly enjoy the evening watching the close-knit, sentimental relationship between mother and son.
Because of the tonal imbalance, Conversations with Mother doesn’t hold together.

cn.t: Critics find this mother-son two-hander a crowd-pleasing tearjerker elevated by Aaron and Doyle's performances, though some dismiss the semi-autobiographical material as calculated sitcom fare that relies too heavily on its talented leads.

vr.q: even if you fall outside of that range, I think there's still a good amount to enjoy here
